title: Practice Exam 2
description: A second full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam.

questions.question: On a highway with a posted maximum of 65 mph, the basic speed law means you:
choices: Must still drive slower if conditions make 65 mph unsafe
May drive 10 mph over if traffic is light
May ignore the limit when roads are clear
questions.explanation: The basic speed law says you may never drive faster than is safe for current conditions, regardless of the posted limit. Rain, traffic, or curves may require a slower speed.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Basic Speed Law

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing without gates or signals, you should not exceed:
questions.explanation: Within 100 feet of a railroad crossing where you cannot see the tracks for 400 feet in both directions, the speed limit is 15 mph.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — 15 mph Speed Limits

questions.question: A round (circular) road sign almost always indicates:
questions.explanation: A round sign is used as a warning for a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down, look, and listen for trains.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sign Shapes

questions.question: A red triangle (downward-pointing) sign means:
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing red and white triangle is a YIELD sign. Slow down and give the right of way to traffic and pedestrians; stop if necessary.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Regulatory Signs

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to:
choices: No one, if you have a green light
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk, even on a green light (unless you have a green arrow).
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Left Turns

questions.question: At an uncontrolled T-intersection, the driver on the road that ends (the stem of the T) must:
choices: Yield to traffic on the through road
questions.explanation: At a T-intersection without signs or signals, traffic on the through road (the top of the T) has the right of way. The driver on the terminating road must yield.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Right-of-Way at Intersections

questions.question: Before changing lanes, the correct order of actions is:
choices: Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, then move
Move, then signal, then check mirrors
Check blind spot only, then move quickly
questions.explanation: Signal your intention, check your mirrors, glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot, and only then change lanes when it is clear.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Changing Lanes

questions.question: A broken white line between lanes means:
choices: Lanes going the same direction; you may change lanes when safe
The lanes go in opposite directions
The road is about to end
questions.explanation: A broken (dashed) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and indicates you may change lanes when it is safe.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Lane Markings

questions.question: The three-second following rule should be increased to four or more seconds when:
choices: Following a motorcycle on a wet road
Driving on a dry, empty road
You are the only car on the highway
You are driving below the speed limit
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions reduce traction or visibility, such as following a motorcycle, driving on wet roads, or in poor weather.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Distance

questions.question: Total stopping distance is made up of:
choices: Only the distance the brakes take to stop the car
Only the speed of the vehicle
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes the distance traveled while you perceive and react to a hazard plus the distance the vehicle travels while braking. Both increase with speed.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Stopping Distances

questions.question: If you have been drinking, the only thing that will sober you up is:
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. Coffee, food, and cold showers do not lower your BAC or make you safe to drive.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol and the Body

questions.question: Driving while using prescription or over-the-counter medication that causes drowsiness is:
choices: Dangerous and can result in a DUI
Always legal because it is prescribed
Fine as long as you drive slowly
Legal if you take less than the dose
questions.explanation: Any drug — legal, prescription, or over-the-counter — that impairs your ability to drive safely can lead to a DUI charge. Check labels for drowsiness warnings.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Drugs and Driving

questions.question: On a two-lane road with a stopped school bus flashing red lights on the opposite side, you must:
choices: Stop, because the road is not divided
Pass only if no children are visible
questions.explanation: On an undivided road, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights. You only continue if a raised divider or median separates the roadways.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Buses

questions.question: Flashing yellow lights on a school zone sign mean:
choices: Slow down; children may be present
You may not enter the area
questions.explanation: Flashing yellow lights at a school zone tell you to slow down and use extra caution because children are likely present.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Zones

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is directly behind you at an intersection, you should:
choices: Clear the intersection, then pull right and stop
Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection
Make a U-turn to avoid it
Speed through the red light ahead
questions.explanation: Never stop in an intersection. Continue through, then pull to the right edge of the road and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: It is illegal to follow within how many feet of a fire truck answering an emergency call?
questions.explanation: You may not follow within 300 feet of any fire engine, police vehicle, ambulance, or other emergency vehicle that has its siren or flashing lights on.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: When you approach a crosswalk and a pedestrian has started to cross, you should:
choices: Stop and let them finish crossing
questions.explanation: You must yield and stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk. Allow them to finish crossing safely before you proceed.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pedestrians

questions.question: Before turning right where a bike lane is present, you should:
choices: Merge into the bike lane within 200 feet of the corner after checking for cyclists
Turn from the regular lane across the bike lane
Never enter the bike lane for any reason
Speed up to turn before any cyclist arrives
questions.explanation: When making a right turn, you may merge into the bike lane within 200 feet of the corner, after signaling and checking that no cyclist is in the way. This avoids cutting across a cyclist's path.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Bicycle Lanes

questions.question: A blue painted curb is reserved for:
questions.explanation: A blue curb indicates parking reserved for persons with disabilities who display a valid placard or license plate.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Colored Curbs

questions.question: When you parallel park, your tires should end up no more than how far from the curb?
questions.explanation: When you finish parallel parking, your wheels should be within 18 inches of the curb.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parallel Parking

questions.question: On the freeway, the far-left lane is generally intended for:
questions.explanation: The left lane is for passing and faster traffic. Slower traffic should keep right, and vehicles preparing to exit should be in the right lanes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Choosing a Lane

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:
choices: Back up on the shoulder to the exit
Stop and wait for a gap to reverse
Make a U-turn across the median
questions.explanation: Never stop or back up on a freeway. If you miss your exit, keep going and use the next one. Backing up causes serious collisions.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Leaving the Freeway

questions.question: Drivers under 18 years of age may use a cell phone while driving:
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 may not use any wireless device while driving, even in hands-free mode, except in a genuine emergency.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Teen Cell Phone Restrictions

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of distracted driving?
choices: Eating, grooming, or adjusting the radio while driving
Keeping both hands on the wheel
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your attention from driving — eating, grooming, reaching for objects, or using a phone. Keep your focus on the road.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Distracted Driving

questions.question: A green arrow pointing left at a traffic signal means:
choices: You may turn left; oncoming traffic is stopped
You must yield to oncoming traffic before turning
You may only turn if a sign permits it
questions.explanation: A green left-turn arrow means you have a protected turn — oncoming traffic is stopped by a red light — so you may turn left, but still watch for pedestrians.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Arrows

questions.question: A red traffic light with a right-turn lane means you may turn right:
choices: After stopping, if it is safe and no sign prohibits it
Only when the light turns green
Only if a green arrow appears
questions.explanation: You may turn right on a red light after coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, unless a sign prohibits the turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Right Turn on Red

questions.question: A flashing yellow arrow at an intersection means:
choices: You may turn, but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
Stop and wait for a green arrow
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means turns are permitted, but you must yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians before completing your turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Flashing Yellow Arrow

questions.question: When can you legally make a U-turn in a residential district?
choices: When there are no vehicles approaching within 200 feet
Only at intersections with a signal
questions.explanation: In a residential area you may make a U-turn when no vehicle is approaching within 200 feet, unless a sign prohibits it. Never make a U-turn near a curve or crest of a hill.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — U-Turns

questions.question: A diamond (◇) symbol painted in a freeway lane indicates:
choices: A lane that is closed ahead
questions.explanation: A white diamond painted on the pavement marks a carpool/HOV lane, which may only be used by vehicles carrying the required number of occupants during posted hours.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Carpool Lanes

questions.question: When parking downhill next to a curb, turn your front wheels:
choices: It does not matter which way
questions.explanation: When parking downhill (with or without a curb), turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the car would roll into the curb if it moved.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on Hills

questions.question: An orange diamond-shaped sign indicates:
choices: A construction or work zone ahead
questions.explanation: Orange signs indicate construction, maintenance, or work zones. Slow down, expect workers and equipment, and obey reduced speed limits.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Construction Zone Signs

questions.question: Fines for traffic violations in a construction zone when workers are present are typically:
questions.explanation: Traffic fines are often doubled in construction or work zones when workers are present. Slow down and drive with extra caution.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Work Zones

questions.question: If you drink alcohol while taking certain medications, the combined effect on driving is usually:
questions.explanation: Combining alcohol with medications can multiply impairment, making driving far more dangerous than either substance alone.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Combining Alcohol and Drugs

questions.question: When a bicyclist is riding ahead of you in a narrow traffic lane, you should:
choices: Slow down and pass only when there is at least 3 feet of clearance
questions.explanation: Treat bicyclists as you would any slow-moving vehicle. Slow down and wait for a safe opportunity to pass with at least 3 feet of clearance.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: When merging into freeway traffic, you should try to enter at a gap that is at least:
questions.explanation: Look for a gap of at least four seconds when merging so you and the vehicles around you have room to adjust safely.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Merging Onto Freeways

questions.question: If your turn signal is still blinking after you complete a turn, you should:
choices: Turn it off manually so you don't mislead other drivers
Leave it on until it stops by itself
Turn on your hazard lights instead
Ignore it; other drivers will understand
questions.explanation: Always make sure your signal turns off after a turn or lane change. A signal left blinking can mislead other drivers into thinking you are about to turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Using Turn Signals
